about.text: A German sour-milk cheese from the northern Harz foothills, though most is now made elsewhere. Crumbly, low-fat sour-milk quark from cow’s milk is shaped and coated with red-smear bacteria, ripening within days into a pungent cheese with under 10% fat in dry matter, often seasoned with caraway.

sources.text: The photograph, its author and its licence, from its page.

how.text: Yeasts eat the lactic acid on the surface and raise its pH; the red-smear bacteria then take over and give the yellow rind and strong smell. The ripening salts neutralise part of the acid first.

sources.text: The table, the facts and the words on how it is made, from these.

steps.note: Table salt (NaCl), sodium bicarbonate (NaHCO₃) and calcium carbonate (CaCO₃) as ripening salts, plus some ripened cheese (Kulturkäse).
Sprayed on with a red-smear culture (Brevibacterium linens).

processing.text: Ripening salts neutralise part of the acid first; the yeasts then raise the surface pH and the red-smear bacteria take over. Some ripened cheese is mixed in. Ripening goes on in the pack, best at 2-4 weeks.

Low-fat quark cheese; ripens 'a few days to a few weeks' (Wikipedia); no protected status

facts.v: In the pack, in the shop and at home; best at 2–4 weeks
5–6 weeks before: mild, white core; 3–4 weeks: aromatic, small white core; 1–2 weeks: strong, no white core
Small round Taler or roll-shaped Stangenkäse; several small loaves sold together as Harzer Roller
